scenario: AITA for visiting my son unannounced. | My son’s(19) in an university. He’s in a different city and lives in an apartment with 2 of his friends. Ever since he left(2 months ago) he just started ignoring me. I didn’t call him excessively, maybe once in two days. He’d hang up or not answer and text me later that he’s busy. Few days ago I was in the city for unrelated reason. I called him because I wanted to visit him but he didn’t answer so I just went to the apartment. His friend answered the door, my son was sleeping. The apartment was filthy, empty bottles everywhere, 5 or more ashtrays filled with cigarette butts. Dirty dishes to the roof. My son woke up and he was surprised when he saw me. He told me that I should’ve called him or something. We talked for a bit and he seemed kinda annoyed. I joked about the place needing a good clean and he just rolled his eyes. I asked him why he was ignoring me. He said that he’s just busy with studying and all that stuff and I should give him space when he needs it. He also said that it was weird that I just showed up unannounced.

prediction.raw: **1** (YTA - *Yes, you're the asshole*) ### Why: - **Respect for boundaries is non negotiable**. Your son is 19 years old, legally an adult, and living independently. His repeated avoidance of calls ( "I'm busy," "text later") is a clear signal that he needs space to establish his own life. Showing up unannounced *despite* this explicitly disrespects his autonomy. - **"Surprise visits" are not okay for adult children**. Even with good intentions (concern about the mess, etc.), the appropriate approach is to *ask* first: "I'm in the city—could I stop by for a quick visit?" If he says no (or doesn't answer), you *must* respect that. - **The "mess" is his responsibility**. As an adult, he gets to decide how he maintains his space. Your judgmental comments about the state of his apartment ( " filthy," " dirty dishes to the roof") added insult to injury. If you're genuinely concerned, *ask* if he needs help cleaning or support—but only * after* he invites you in. - **His reaction was entirely justified**. He explicitly said " it was weird that I just showed up unannounced"—and he's right. This is a standard boundary violation in any healthy parent-adult-child relationship. ### What to do differently next time: - **Text first**: "Hey, I'm in [ city] for work. Would you be open to a quick coffee or a 10-minute visit? No pressure if you're swamped." - **Accept " no" gracefully**. If he says no or doesn't respond, *drop it*. Pushing further will only damage trust. - **Remember: adulthood means letting go**. Your role now is to *support* him, not *manage* him. His messy apartment, while frustrating, is his to navigate. Your job is to be a safe, non judgmental presence when * he* reaches out—not a surveillance agent. > 💡 **Key insight**: A " good parent" at this stage isn't the one who shows up unannounced to " fix" things. It's the one who *trusts* their child to figure things out on their own terms. > *—This is a 1 (YTA) because your actions violated his boundaries, ignored his clear signals, and added unnecessary stress to a situation he's already managing.*
